item.title: About this blog....
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Being outdoor and going camping is one of the most important things I like to do. I started this blog because I was looking for a way to keep track of places I visited, where I would go again, which place I would avoid and to share my experience. We (me and my family) usually go camping every 3 to 4 weeks, we started when my oldest son was 1 year old. My second son had his first camping trip and road trip from the bay area to Death Valley when he was 6 Month old. If you have questions or comments, feel free to comment, or contact me. In the Menu are some Categories: National Parks: You can look through my blog entries Park by Park State Parks: You can look through my blog entries State Park by State Park Campgrounds: All Campgrounds are listed here Maps: You find different maps I created with links to the blog entires Hikes: All Hike blogs are in this category.

item.title: Trip 01 · Valley of Fire
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
TRIP 01 - NEVADA - ~520 MILES - 3-4 DAYS

Valley of Fire State Park

Nevada's oldest state park - blazing red Aztec sandstone formations, ancient petroglyphs, and alien landscapes just an hour from Las Vegas.

DISTANCE

~520 mi

DAYS

3-4 days

VEHICLE NEEDED

Any stock SUV/truck

BEST SEASON

Oct - Apr

Route Map

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1Xp5jm7Coq0A96tolFgZ6o9hIT8d-TRE&ehbc=2E312F&w=1200&h=600]
Open Route in Google Maps

Explore by Theme

⛺
Camping 🏜
Activities 🥾
Hikes ℹ️
Tips & Logistics

Camping Options

Two campgrounds inside the park, both surrounded by red rock - or fall back to Las Vegas for a no-camp version.

Atlatl Rock CampgroundIn-park with hookups — ~44 sites at the base of the petroglyph rock; power & water, showers, dump station. Book on Reserve Nevada — winter/spring weekends fill fast. Arch Rock CampgroundIn-park primitive — smaller and quieter, sites tucked into red sandstone coves. No hookups — the more scenic tent choice. Las Vegas BaseHotel fallback 1 hr from the park — good for shoulder-season heat or a shower night.

Activities

Scenic DriveNV-169 Scenic Byway and Mouse's Tank Road. Petroglyphs at Atlatl RockAncient Native American rock art up a staircase viewing platform. Wildlife SpottingBighorn sheep, roadrunners, kit foxes. Sunrise & Sunset PhotographyThe best light in the park — golden hour on red rock. Lake Mead Day TripNational Recreation Area, 30 min east.

Hikes

Five Canyon Overlook1 mi · easy · ~45 min — sandy trail to the Fire Canyon overlook, best in late-afternoon light. Rainbow Vista Trail1 mi · easy · ~25 min — colorful sandstone bowl with 360° canyon views. Open year-round. Petroglyph Canyon / Mouse's Tank0.7 mi · easy · ~30–45 min — narrow red canyon packed with petroglyphs. Silica Dome0.9 mi · easy · ~22 min — light scramble to the white dome, views over Fire Canyon and Lake Mead. Fire Wave & Pink Canyon2 mi · easy · ~50 min — iconic swirling slickrock plus pink slot canyon. Best at sunrise. Closed Jun–Oct. White Domes Trail1.1 mi · moderate · ~30–45 min — loop through a slot canyon and 1966 movie-set ruins. Hike clockwise. Closed mid-May–Sep.

Tips & Logistics

Entry Fee$15/vehicle for non-NV residents. Start EarlyOn the trail by 7am in shoulder seasons. WaterBring 3L+ per person per hike. Offline MapDownload the NV State Parks offline map before arriving. Fuel UpGas up before entering — no services inside the park. Avoid SummerJune–August regularly hits 110°F+ — plan Oct–Apr.
Back to All Trips

item.title: Trip 02 - Calico Ghost Town and Off-Road
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
TRIP 02 - MOJAVE DESERT, CA - ~390 MILES - 2-3 DAYS

Calico Ghost Town and Off-Road Trails

An 1881 silver mining ghost town in the Calico Mountains surrounded by some of Southern California's best OHV trails - rock crawls, canyon runs, and desert arches.

DISTANCE

~390 mi

DAYS

2-3 days

VEHICLE NEEDED

Stock 4x4 (lifted for crawls)

BEST SEASON

Oct - Apr

Route Map

Open Route in Google Maps

Explore by Theme

⛺
Camping ⛏️
Activities 🚙
Off-Road Trails & Hikes ℹ️
Tips & Logistics

Camping Options

Camping right at the ghost town is the move - you're steps from the trails and entry is included.

Calico Ghost Town Campground265 sites below the town — full hookups, showers, fire rings; camping includes ghost-town entry. Reserve via San Bernardino County Parks — holiday/event weekends fill up. BLM Dispersed · Mule / Owl CanyonFree primitive camping on surrounding BLM land — no services, pack everything out. Owl Canyon Campground (~30 min) is the developed budget alternative. Barstow Hotels10 minutes away — chain hotels, gas, groceries. The no-camp fallback.

Activities

Maggie Mine TourDescend into an original 1880s silver mine. Narrow Gauge RailroadRide the Calico & Odessa line around the town. Gold PanningTry your luck on-site. Mystery ShackThe gravity-illusion attraction. Calico–Vegas OHV RunThe annual off-road event, if the timing lines up. Elmer's Bottle Tree RanchQuirky Route 66 folk-art stop en route.

Off-Road Trails & Hikes

Trail ratings and condition updates from Trails Offroad - Calico Region.

Calico Ghost Town Walk0.7 mi · easy · 2–3 hrs — main street, schoolhouse, mine and saloon of the 1881 silver town. Mule Canyon~2 mi RT · easy–moderate · ~1 hr — colorful intro trail; a Kill Bill 2 filming location. Wall Street Canyon~4 mi RT · moderate 4x4 · ~2 hrs — stunning canyon walls with overlook; 4WD and 33" tires. Kramer Arch~3 mi RT · hard 4x4 · ~2 hrs — stone arch just big enough to squeeze a vehicle through; high-clearance 4x4 required. Odessa Canyon~4 mi RT · extreme 4x4 · ~3 hrs — the flagship Calico trail: 7-foot waterfall, rollover spot, tight off-camber canyon. Calico OHV Open RidingMiles of trails · varies · half–full day — ATVs, UTVs, dirt bikes welcome; green/red sticker required.

Tips & Logistics

Entry Fee~$8/adult — free with overnight camping. OHV StickersGreen/red sticker required; ATVs and UTVs allowed. Red-sticker OHVs Oct–Jun only. VehicleHigh-clearance 4x4 needed for Kramer Arch and the canyon trails. Supplies in Barstow3 mi away — gas, groceries and hotel options. Avoid SummerJune–September Mojave heat is brutal — plan Oct–Apr.
Back to All Trips

item.title: Trip 03 - White Rim Road Canyonlands
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
TRIP 03 - CANYONLANDS, UTAH - ~850 MILES - 4-5 DAYS - HIGH-CLEARANCE 4WD

White Rim Road - Canyonlands

A 100-mile loop around the Island in the Sky mesa in Canyonlands National Park - one of the most spectacular multi-day 4x4 routes in the American West.

DISTANCE

~850 mi

DAYS

4-5 days

VEHICLE NEEDED

HC 4WD + low range

BEST SEASON

Mar-May, Sep-Nov

DOGS

Not Allowed

Route Map

Open Route in Google Maps

Explore by Theme

⛺
Camping & Permits 🏜
Activities 🥾
Hikes & Viewpoints ℹ️
Tips & Logistics

Camping & Permits

Camping on the White Rim is permit-only backcountry - your overnight permit IS your campsite reservation, so this is the first thing to book.

Overnight PermitBook on recreation.gov up to 4 months ahead — spring and fall weekends go instantly. Book this FIRST. Designated Sites Only10 camping areas / 20 sites along the route — no dispersed camping, no water, pack-out toilet system required. White CrackBest halfway camp on a 2-day run — sweeping views toward the Needles district. Murphy Hogback & GooseberryAlternative 2-day camps — Murphy sits on the rim after a steep climb, 360° mesa views. Labyrinth CampsAdd these Green River overlook sites for a 3-day itinerary. Before & AfterMoab hotels, or Horsethief Campground on the mesa top near the Mineral Bottom exit.

Activities

Shafer Trail SwitchbacksThe dramatic 1,400 ft descent that starts the loop. Musselman ArchWalk across the roadside arch — sheer drops on both sides. Lathrop CanyonSide road down to the Colorado River — great lunch spot. StargazingCanyonlands is a certified International Dark Sky Park. Mesa-Top SunriseGreen River Overlook or Mesa Arch — before or after the loop. Monument BasinPhotography stop — towering spires straight out of a western.

Hikes & Viewpoints Along the Route

Hiking trail links via AllTrails. Full White Rim road guide on Trails Offroad.

White Rim Overlook Trail1.8 mi RT · easy — flat trail to a mesa-edge overlook with Colorado River views; best late afternoon. Fort Bottom Ruin Trail3.4 mi RT · moderate · 511 ft gain — ancient ruin and Green River viewpoint, from Fort Bottom campsite. Monument Basin ViewpointRoadside — towering sandstone spires rising from the canyon floor. Musselman ArchRoadside — natural sandstone arch you can walk across, sheer-drop canyon views. White CrackRoadside campsite — the best halfway stop, views toward the Needles. Murphy HogbackShort steep climb — rim campsites with 360° mesa views.

Tips & Logistics

Base in MoabGreat restaurants, gear shops and hotels before and after the loop. Vehicle RequirementsHigh-clearance 4WD with low range mandatory — Wrangler/4Runner-class minimum; no AWD crossovers, no ATVs/UTVs. All-terrain tires highly recommended. Height limit 10 ft. No Water on RouteBring everything you need for the full loop. No Cell ServiceDownload offline maps before dropping in. Travel in GroupsA tow off the White Rim can cost $2,000+. Shafer Canyon EntrySteep switchbacks; impassable when wet — check conditions with the park first. Avoid SummerCanyon temps exceed 110°F — go Mar–May or Sep–Nov.
Back to All Trips

item.title: Trip 04 - Lost Coast Overland Route
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
TRIP 04 - NORTHERN CALIFORNIA - ~220 MILES - 2-4 DAYS

Lost Coast Overland Route

A 160-mile overland route through old growth redwood forests, the King Range, and California's most remote coastline.

DISTANCE

~220 mi

DAYS

2-4 days

VEHICLE NEEDED

High clearance - 4x4 rec.

BEST SEASON

Late May - Oct

Route Map

Open Route in Google Maps

Explore by Theme

⛺
Camping 🌲
Activities 🥾
Hikes 🛻
Route Highlights ℹ️
Tips & Logistics

Camping Options

Primitive beachside camping is the whole point out here - no hookups anywhere, and that's exactly right. No permit needed for vehicle camping (unlike the backpacking trail).

Usal Beach CampgroundDesignated sites on the black sand beach at the end of Usal Road — first-come, self-register, no services. The crown jewel camp of the trip; no beach driving. Nadelos & Wailaki (BLM)Small, quiet creekside BLM camps in the southern King Range near Shelter Cove — vault toilets, small fee. Mattole Beach (BLM)At the Mattole River mouth near Petrolia — windy, wild, and the trailhead for the Punta Gorda Lighthouse hike. A.W. Way County ParkGrassy riverside sites near Petrolia — the gentler option if the coast is blowing a gale. Shelter CoveInns and an RV park in the one town on the coast — good first or last night.

Activities

Drive Usal RoadMendocino Rd 431 — the narrow dirt road from Highway 1 through the Sinkyone Wilderness. Mattole RoadThrough Petrolia and Honeydew — alternating paved and dirt with huge coastal views. Roosevelt ElkWildlife spotting in the Sinkyone Wilderness. Beachcombing & TidepoolingOn the black sand beaches — check the tide tables first. King Range OHV TrailsSteep switchbacks, creek crossings, mountain views. Avenue of the GiantsDay trip — 31 miles of old-growth redwoods. Stargazing & Digital DetoxThere's no cell service to tempt you.

Hikes

Punta Gorda Lighthouse~6.5 mi RT · moderate — beach walk from Mattole to the abandoned 1911 lighthouse; elephant seals haul out nearby. Time it for low tide. Black Sands BeachAs far as you like · easy — iconic black sand stretch at Shelter Cove; walk north toward the wilderness beach. Sinkyone Bluff Trails1–4 mi · easy–moderate — short trails from Usal Beach camp up onto the coastal bluffs; whales in season. King Peak~5 mi RT · strenuous — 4,088 ft summit rising almost straight out of the ocean; the biggest view on the Lost Coast.

Route Highlights

Mattole RoadScenic drive winding through Petrolia and Honeydew — alternates paved and unpaved with stunning coastal vistas. Usal BeachRemote black sand beach — camp in designated sites; no beach driving permitted. Sinkyone Wilderness SPDramatic coastal bluffs and old growth forests — watch for Roosevelt elk. King Range OHV TrailsSteep switchbacks, creek crossings, and rock-strewn paths through the mountains. Shelter CoveRemote coastal community — good base before heading into the backcountry. Avenue of the GiantsHumboldt Redwoods day trip — 31-mile drive through old-growth coastal redwoods.

Tips & Logistics

SeasonLate May to October — Usal Road is gated during the wet season. Check Mendocino County road closure status before going. VehicleHigh clearance needed everywhere; 4WD strongly recommended on Usal Road — steep, narrow, muddy when damp. Fuel Up FirstFill up in Garberville or Fortuna — no fuel in the backcountry. No Cell ServiceDownload offline maps — no coverage throughout. No Permit NeededVehicle camping needs no permit — unlike the backpacking version of the Lost Coast Trail. Dogs WelcomeAllowed on leash throughout this route.
Back to All Trips

item.title: Montana de Oro SP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: We went to Montana de Oro State Park over Labor Day Weekend. The campground is away from the street, you just hear the waves from the ocean. The beach is in walking distance and there are a lot of hiking and mountain bike trails very close to the campground. Once arrived you don't need a car. If you arrive at night you get a campsite assigned, when you arrive during the day you can choose your site. Campsides are are good sized and very open, don't expect a lot of privacy. There are some large trees for some shade, however some sides have full sun all day. The streets are paved and kids can ride bikes and scooters. - Would I go there again? Yes.

item.title: Yosemite NP: Lower Pine Campground
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Yosemite Valley Campgrounds book out really quick. The lower pine campground is large with little to no privacy. I would try to get a site more in the back of the campground, otherwise everyone who comes in and out, passes your tent. You have a lot of RVs with generators. If you like easy camping, with restaurants and stores close by the campgrounds are ok. Yosemite valley is always crowded. - Would I go there again? No, I rather would go to camp 4, a little farther west, but since it is a walk in campground, there are no RV's.

item.title: Yosemite NP: Wawona Campground
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
This campground won't fill up within seconds like most of the campgrounds in Yosemite. At least not when I booked for Memorial Day Weekend. Most of the sides are very private, especially site no. 037! As you can see on the picture the other tents are farther away and higher. The area around site no. 037 is free of RV's.
The side is away from the campsite road, close to a river. The kids loved to play at the river bed all day long. The campground also has a little beach at the river.
The campground is great to explore the south part of Yosemite. Would I go there again? Yes.

item.title: Red Rock Canyon State Park
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: I only drove by on my way to Death Valley, but this State Park is on my "Places to go" List.

item.title: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Death Valley National Park is worth to go there. There is so much to explore and see. I never thought that a dessert can be so colorful. You can go hiking in a lot of different canyons. Drive through a canyon or to the sailing rocks. Run over sand dunes. The best time to go is spring and fall. There will be some more blog entries about specific thinks I did there.

item.title: Sailing Rocks and Tea Cattle Junction in Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: It took us 2h, to drive down the off road to the sailing rocks. It was amazing to see these large rocks with their scratch marks in the dried out lake. Even during Spring, it was very hot. Just be aware that there are rattlesnakes, we heard one closer to the mountains.

item.title: Titus Canyon: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: You can drive through Titus Canyon in Death Valley, it is a 27 mi long dirt road. It takes a couple of hours, since it is beautiful and you can not drive very fast, you want to do a lot of stops and enjoy the scenery. You drive along a ghost town, narrow canyons and you'll see petroglyphs.

item.title: Golden Canyon Trail: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This is an easy hike, since you are in the dessert, start early and bring plenty of water. There is not much shade on this hiking. It is an easy hike, mostly flat, with a lot of different shaped canyons around you. We saw one roadrunner. You can also drive to Zabriskie Point to see the Canyon from the top.

item.title: Ubhebe Crater: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: It was amazing for me to see how many different faces Death Valley has. When I heard the word dessert, I had always the Sahara in mind. The different places in this National Park thought me how wrong I was. I never expected so many different colors and plants in a dessert.

item.title: Borax Works Interpretive Trail: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This is at the beginning of the Haromy Borax Works Interpretive Trail. I enjoyed taking pictures there a lot.

item.title: Mesquite spring campground: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This campground is at the north part of Death Valley, very close to zu Uhebe Crater. The sites are very open, you don't have privacy, and sun the whole day. There is a river bed next to the campground, it was dry when we were there in april.

item.title: Rhyolite Ghost Town: Death Valley NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This is a very small but unique ghost town, on the east side of Death Valley NP. There are a few houses, one has a wall build out of glass bottles.

item.title: The Narrows Canyon hike: Zion NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: We went to Zion NP on our way to the Grand Canyon, we planned on being one day in the park. Basically we drove through with a lot of stops, and did one hike. Be prepared for this hike, you are going to walk in the water a lot, one area was about 1m deep. I was happy to wear shoes which covered my toes. I also used hiking poles, they saved me a couple times from getting out of balance and falling in the water completely. I carried one of my boys on my back, he was able to stay dry all the time. This is a park where I want to go back to explore more.

item.title: Bredoo Canyon Road: Joshua Tree NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: We never tried a dirt road before, and were so exited to made it over the sand road to the canyon entrance. When we looked down to see how the road looked like, we decided not to go any further. I would have loved to see it, but we were not prepared enough for that. It was still a great drive through the park.

item.title: Cholla Cactus Garden: Joshua Tree NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Driving into a dessert and seeing more and more cactus is impressive, but I didn't expect to see so many of them at one place:

item.title: Close Up Views: Joshua Tree NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Here are some of my favorite pictures of this park. I like to photograph patterns, structures and close ups a lot. Don't be surprised to see more pictures like this.

item.title: "Screen Time is over"
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
I like to be outdoor with my family, and my kids enjoy camping a lot. But to get to the beautiful places it often involves a long ride in the car. Like most kids, my kids love to play iPad or watch a movie in the car. But I don’t want them to play on the iPad the whole time when we have a 15h trip in front of us. This is my solution for keeping kids happy in the car when I say “screen time is over" Picture of a full set up And this is how I did it. First, you need to figure out how you can use the space in your car between or around your kids best, that nothing flies around. For my car I used a plastic container with 3 drawers and a wooden box on top. I tried different types of boxes, but they all broke somehow, and did not last long. The wooden box is strapped to both seats, that it stays in place. I have a huge variety of different activities, and exchange them before we hit the road. Before a long road trip I usually have one surprise for each kid. Books: Usually I go to the library one day before the road trip, that we have books with us the kids don't know yet. There are also good iBooks in the library or for free in the app store or iBook library. Here are my favorite: Kids Versus - Sea Otter - Music: When screen time is over, I still allow my kids to listen to music, don't forget headphones. Coloring books:I don't want to bring a lot of coloring books, with the same character, I feel like they get easily tired of it. Here are my favorite coloring books: Usborne books Activity binder: This binder has a lot of potential, and this it what I have in it:
  • Plain paper, paper with lines, paper with cross lines.
  • Print out coloring pages and activity sheets. Since their interest changes, it is easy to print out what they like the most before a trip.
  • Road Trip Bingo Bingos
  • Laminated sheets with Road (I will explain that later)
  • Laminated sheets with People (I will explain that later)
Magnet toys and a cookie sheet: Flash Cards Reusable Activity Cards Garbage, Tissues and Wipes Mini Cars

item.title: Explore the World
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
Explore the World

Off-road overland routes, city tours, and everything in between - the places we've been and the ones we're still planning.

All Destinations

Off-road routes and city tours - every adventure on one map. Click any pin to explore the trip.

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1cyj76LPo8WGqPXVQ2v4HgTAcapAKz7E&ehbc=2E312F&w=1200&h=600]

Off-Road Adventures

Trip 01 · Valley of FireNevada · ~520 mi · 3-4 days - blazing red sandstone, petroglyphs, alien desert an hour from Vegas. Any stock SUV or truck · best Oct-Apr. Trip 02 · Calico Ghost TownMojave, CA · ~390 mi · 2-3 days - an 1881 silver ghost town ringed by SoCal's best OHV trails. Stock 4x4; lifted rig only for the crawls · best Oct-Apr. Trip 03 · White Rim RoadCanyonlands, UT · ~850 mi · 4-5 days - the legendary 100-mile mesa loop. HC 4WD + low range required, permit needed, no dogs · best Mar-May & Sep-Nov. Trip 04 · Lost Coast OverlandN. California · ~220 mi · 2-4 days - redwoods, the King Range and beach camps on the remotest coast. High clearance, 4x4 for Usal Rd · late May-Oct.

City Tours

Not every adventure needs a dirt road - exploring the world's great cities, one guide at a time.

London & BeyondLandmarks, markets, museums and day trips across London and beyond. City Tour 02 · BerlinThe Berlin guide is on its way over - history, museums and the wall, coming soon.

Camping Set-Ups

Every trip card above says what it really takes - short version: Valley of Fire works in any stock SUV or truck. Calico wants a stock high-clearance 4x4 (a lifted rig with low range only if you're doing the rock crawls). White Rim requires true high-clearance 4WD with low range - park rules, no AWD crossovers. Lost Coast needs high clearance, with 4x4 strongly recommended for Usal Road in the dry season.

TruckPickup with a rooftop tent or bed camper - hauls all the gear and handles every trip on this site. Jeep Rubicon · LiftedLow range, lockers and clearance - the set-up for White Rim and the rock-crawl loops. SUVA stock high-clearance SUV covers Valley of Fire and the main trails - tent camping from the trunk. Camper VanComfort at basecamp - great for the developed campgrounds; leave the rough trails to a 4x4.

item.title: London & Beyond
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
Our family week in London - the plan day by day, plus everything we picked grouped by theme.

Trip Map

[googlemaps https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1nspSJgnDu-cATW9y1h5DRp29o1M2uP4&ehbc=2E312F&w=1200&h=600]

Explore by Theme

Attractions Museums Neighborhoods Food & Drink Day Trips Cars Shopping Audio Tours Good to know

Day by Day

Day 1 · Arrival & Thames Walk Day 2 · Bletchley Park Day 3 · Dover Day 4 · Westminster & West End Day 5 · Belfast & the Dungeon Day 6 · Palace, War Rooms & Museum Day 7 · The Tower & the West End Day 8 · St Paul’s Cathedral Additional Things to Do

Day 1 · Arrival & Thames Walk

A packed first day on foot, in the order we actually walked it: a morning coffee, then the covered markets - Old Spitalfields, Leadenhall, and Borough - lunch at the Art Nouveau Blackfriar, Lower Marsh market, the Leake Street graffiti tunnel, and the London Eye, ending along the South Bank at the Oxo Tower and dinner at The Alchemist Bevis Marks.
Walked: 8.8 miles.

Spitalfields MarketOld Spitalfields - a covered market of food stalls, vintage, and crafts. Leadenhall MarketThe ornate Victorian arcade - a Diagon Alley filming spot. Borough MarketLunch stop - London's best-loved food market. The BlackfriarA jewel-box Art Nouveau pub by Blackfriars - marble, mosaics, and lunch on the terrace. Lower MarshWaterloo’s characterful street market - indie food stalls and vintage. The Graffiti TunnelLeake Street Arches - London's legal street-art tunnel under Waterloo. London EyeThe riverside big wheel - panoramic views over the Thames. The Alchemist Bevis MarksA theatrical cocktail bar to end the day, back in the City.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 2 · Bletchley Park

The codebreaker day - ~40 minutes by train from Euston to Bletchley Park (Hut 8, The Mansion, and The National Museum of Computing) - then back to London for Camden Lock Market and an evening in the pubs.
Walked: 6.4 miles.

Bletchley ParkThe WWII codebreaking estate: Hut 8, the Mansion, and more, ~40 min by train from Euston. The National Museum of ComputingThe working Bombe and Colossus rebuilds, same campus. Camden Lock MarketBack in London - canal-side stalls and street food.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 3 · Dover

Train from St Pancras to Dover (~1 hr): the White Cliffs and Dover Castle with its Secret Wartime Tunnels, then back to London for dinner at Dishoom Shoreditch and a pub.
Walked: 11.5 miles.

White Cliffs of DoverThe clifftop walk past Langdon Beach - France on the horizon. Dover CastleThe great keep and the Secret Wartime Tunnels (Operation Dynamo) - book online for 10% off. Dishoom ShoreditchBombay-style dinner back in London - bacon naan rolls and black daal. The MinoriesA traditional pub by Tower Hill to round off the day.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 4 · Westminster & the West End

Westminster landmarks into the West End: Big Ben and Westminster Abbey, Trafalgar and Leicester Squares, shopping on Carnaby and Oxford Street (with the giant LEGO store), The Clink, and drinks with a view at Sky Garden.
Walked: 7.8 miles.

Big BenThe clock tower and Houses of Parliament, best from the riverside. Westminster AbbeyThe coronation church, almost 1,000 years of royal history. Trafalgar SquareNelson's Column and the lions, with the National Gallery next door. LEGO Store Leicester SquareThe world’s biggest LEGO store, with M&M’s World next door. Carnaby StreetIndie fashion and streetwear in Soho's most colorful lane. SohoWandering the West End’s liveliest quarter - bars, cafés, and neon. Oxford & Regent StreetThe flagship shopping mile - Selfridges, Nike Town and every brand you can name. The Clink Prison MuseumOn the site of one of England’s oldest prisons, on Bankside (ticketed). Sky GardenRooftop garden 155 m up - free entry (book ahead), bars and restaurants at the top.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 5 · HMS Belfast & the Dungeon

A riverside day by the Thames: the London Dungeon and HMS Belfast, Tower Bridge, and a stretch of the Roman London Wall - finishing with an evening walk around the Tower of London and Tower Bridge lit up.
Walked: 7.1 miles.

The London DungeonTheatrical, spooky-fun ride through London’s dark history. HMS BelfastWWII cruiser moored by Tower Bridge, nine decks to explore. Tower BridgeThe Victorian bascule bridge - up close on the evening riverside loop. London WallSurviving stretches of the Roman city wall near Tower Hill.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 6 · Palace, War Rooms & Museum

A royal-and-history day: Buckingham Palace and the Changing of the Guard, a wander through St James’s Park with a café stop, the Churchill War Rooms, and the British Museum - ending with a night walk along the Thames.
Walked: 7.4 miles.

Buckingham PalaceThe exterior and the free Changing of the Guard (most days ~11:00). St James’s ParkThe royal park’s lake and pelicans, with a lakeside café stop - the classic view back to the palace. Churchill War RoomsThe untouched WWII bunker under Westminster. The British MuseumRosetta Stone, mummies, the Parthenon sculptures. Free. Thames Night WalkAn evening stroll along the river - the city lit up on the water.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 7 · The Tower & the West End

The last full day: Covent Garden, the Tower of London, dinner at SUSHISAMBA, and Les Misérables in the West End to finish - with Piccadilly Circus lit up along the way.
Walked: 6.5 miles.

Covent GardenThe piazza and covered market - street performers and the Apple Market. Tower of LondonCrown Jewels, Beefeaters, and ravens (best early afternoon). SUSHISAMBA LondonDinner out - Japanese-Brazilian-Peruvian sharing plates. Les MisérablesThe world’s longest-running musical at the Sondheim Theatre (Delfont Mackintosh). Our evening finale. Piccadilly CircusThe bright lights - the West End’s neon crossroads.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Day 8 · St Paul’s Cathedral

A final morning before heading home: St Paul’s Cathedral and lunch at Gordon Ramsay’s Bread Street Kitchen & Bar.
Walked: 5.3 miles.

St. Paul’s CathedralWren’s dome - the climb to the Whispering Gallery and city views. Bread Street Kitchen & BarGordon Ramsay’s all-day restaurant at One New Change, right by St Paul’s.
↑ Back to Day by Day

Additional Things to Do

Nothing here has a fixed day - these are the if-there’s-time extras and flexible stops we pick from as we go. Markets and food happen wherever each day takes us.

National GalleryFree world-class art on Trafalgar Square - including the Skyfall painting. Abbey Road Pedestrian CrossingThe Beatles crosswalk outside Abbey Road Studios. item.excerpt:encoded: Our family city tour of London - attractions, museums, neighborhoods, day trips, car stops, walking tours, and the booking checklist.

item.title: Joshua Tree NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Joshua Tree National Park was the second National Park I went to after starting our camping trips. The campgrounds inside the Park are "first come first serve". We were lucky, we went over Memorial Day weekend, arrived at about 12pm, and got one of the last spots. You can make a reservation at  Indian Cove campground on the north side of the park, if you like to know wether you have a spot or not.

item.title: Joshua Tree NP: Campground Hidden Valley
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This is a first come first serve campground, with very private sites. You have Rocks and plants around the campsites, with small paths to your neighbors. You can go and start climbing and walking around the huge rocks right from your campsite. Be aware that there is no water on this campground. Would I go again? Yes, the night sky was amazing and you are in the middle of the park.

item.title: Joshua Tree NP: Campground Indian Cove
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This is a large Campground, on the north side of Joshua Tree Park. You can make reservations in advance. The sites are very open and you don't have a lot of privacy. It is nice to have stores close by, but it is is a 40 min drive into the park. Would I go again: yes, especially when I think it could be hard to get a spot inside the park.

item.title: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Yosemite National Park is my favorite National Park. The views even just from driving through the park are amazing. Most of the times I visited I was in the Valley, now I try to go to a different area and do different hikes. My most success in Yosemite was, being on top of Half Dome.

item.title: Vernal and Nevada Fall Hike: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
The first part until the bridge, where you can see Vernal Fall, is paved and very easy. From the bridge until the bottom of Vernal Fall, it starts going up, but the steepest part, is the end, you have a lot of stairs to climb. To go to the top of Nevada Fall is the same difficulty, there are not as many stairs at the end, but switchbacks. You have the choice of going the same way back, or you can take the John Muir Trail back, this trail is longer, but not as steep.

Hike to Vernal Fall:

item.title: Half Dome Hike: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
You hike up Nevada and Vernal Fall and just keep going..... You are passing little Yosemite valley, a backpacker camp. From there you have a lot of shade, because the trail is between a lot of trees. It goes up constantly, but not as steep as the last part of Vernal and Nevada Fall. I did not believe it until I saw it, but there was a ranger who was checking if you have a permit. After that it is still 1 mi to go. You see Half Dome coming closer the whole way. And then you are in front of the Sub Dome, it is like going up Nevada Fall again, in the sun. After that, I was just happy to finally see the cables. And I made it up there.
You see Half Dome a couple times during the Hike
...and Half dome is coming closer...
...but first comes Sub Dome...
and finally the cables
on top of Half Dome

item.title: Glacier Point Hike: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
A hike with a lot of switch backs, and even more great views of the Valley. We did this hike in October 2004, Yosemite Fall was completely dry, and there was only a little water at Nevada and Vernal fall.
The Trail
The Views

item.title: Housekeeping Camp: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
My very first night in Yosemite was in 2004 in Housekeeping camp. It was my first time in the US, we underestimated the drive from the Bay Area, and arrived at around 8 or 9pm. It was dark, and we had no idea how we are going to find out "tent". We were very pleased and surprised to find an envelope with our name, with a map and direction on how to find out site. Unfortunately it was occupied. But there were enough very nice people there who helped us to find an empty tent. And immediately we got warned that every night bears are coming into the camp. I was very scared about that and did not leave my husband off my side. I think it was the second night, were I woke up because of a very strong smell: It smelled like I am in the zoo. The bear was in the camp, and we saw him running away. However, we also had a small visitor at night sitting on our table, the evidence is on the picture. Housekeeping Camp is a great place to stay. The "tent's" are for up to 4 people, you have your own little patio with a picnic table and fire pit.
Racon Footbrints on our table
the "tents's"this was my first impression when I woke up
Housekeeping camp from Glacier Point

item.title: Yosemite Fall Hike: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
This is another hike with a lot of switch backs. You get nice views of the valley and sometimes of black bears (we saw one). The last part of the trail is exposed to the sun. There are a lot of little ponds up there to dip your feed in (far away from the edge). At least when I was there in fall with not so much water....
Yosemite Fall
view into the valley
on top of yosemite fall
the edge
a pond far away from the edge

item.title: Tenaya Lake: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: You can not drive up Tioga pass without a stop at Tenaya Lake. There are beautiful beaches, and the water is always refreshing. It is a great place to make a stop for a picknick or just for relax and enjoy the surroundings. Kayaking on the lake is also a lot of fun.

item.title: Tioga Pass: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
Tioga Pass in Yosemite is a bringing you to a higher elevated area of the park. You are overviewing the park and you have far views in the distant. Tenaya Lake is worth a stop.
I believe this is half dome
Tenaya Lake

item.title: Yosemite NP in white
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Even in Winter, Yosemite is a great place to go. It is much more quiet and not as busy as in the summer month. The kids loved it to get pulled on the sled and you should bring spikes for your shoes. They also sell them in the stores in the Valley.

item.title: Hetch Hetchy: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: It is hard to believe that Hetch Hetchy was once a Valley like Yosemity Valley. There is one day Trail along the lake, we hiked until we reached the waterfall. We started on a day with clouds, when we reached the waterfall we had rain and hail. This is a very easy hike.

item.title: Waterwheel Falls: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This hike shows you how diverse Yosemite can be. You hike over meadows, through forests, along the Tuolumne Rive, over large flat rock areas and down waterfalls. You can go swimming in the river, the only part I did not like is, that you hike downhill first, and the way back is uphill.

item.title: Swinging Bridge Hike: Yosemite NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: A very easy hike outside Yosemite on the south side. It is flat and a great hike with kids, since they can swim in the water.

item.title: Kayaking at Moss Landing
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: If you time the tides right, this is a very easy kayaking tour. You start at the ocean and kayak land inwards. There are a lot of seals, otter, pelicans and birds. Some seals are even diving under your Kayak and playing with you. There is a Kayak rental and if you like to enjoy Moss Landing without paddling, you can also do a guided boat tour.

item.title: Tide Pools: Point Lobos SP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: My kids love walking around tide pools and looking for animals. Point Lobos is a great place for that. You don't need to hike to get there, the parking lot is very close by. We also saw a lot of Whales passing by.

item.title: Wilder Ranch SP: Old Cove Landing Trail
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This 2.5 mi hike shows you similar views like you get when you drive down coast highway 1, but the trail is away from the street. There are great spots for a picknick and Whale watching.

item.title: Lassen NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
Lassen is a Volcanic National Park, with lots of volcanoes, meadows, forests and mountain lakes. You are able to see a lot of the park just by driving through and doing short hikes. There is also a Lake with Kayak rental close by.
bumpass hellred cinder conepilot pinnaclebroke off mountain trailview from broke of mountain to lassen peakThings we did in Lassen NP

item.title: Red Cinder Cone Hike: Lassen NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
This was my first time on top of a volcano. You can hike all the way up to the top and look into the crater. It was exhausting, because you hike on volcano rocks, you can compare it with walking on a sandy beach. You are in the sun the whole time, but it is worth a trip to the top.
on top of red cinder conered cinder cone on top of red cinder cone

item.title: Broke off Mountain Hike: Lassen NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
This hike was crazy, since I did not know what to expect and we had both kids with us. My husband chose and didn't tell me the part with the elevation. I think the older one was hiking for maybe the first half mile, the rest of this 7.4mi hike with 2600ft elevation gain, he had fun on my back, talking to me and sleeping in-between. I made it to the top and back, afterwards my husband believed me, that I am capable of hiking up Half Dome (we did one year later). Broke off Mountain is a trail with great views over Lassen and the Surroundings.
top of broke off mountainview from the top to lassen peakthe last switchback of the trailthe last part of the trail

item.title: Grand Canyon NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Grand Canyon National Park was our second Road Trip with both kids. For me a Road trip is a tour, longer then 3 nights and more then 1000mi. We only had a couple of days, but I think the pictures say enough. We hiked down the south kaibab trail down until Skeleton Point (without kids). You get great views inside the Canyon. We enjoyed the sunset at Yaki point.

item.title: Clear Lake SP: Campground
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Depending on the time of the year, the Lake is not always clear! We went over Labor Day Weekend, and it was completely green, it was still safe to go into the water, but not as much fun as with clear water. There are two campsites on this campground which I recommend (58 and 59). Those are the only two sites where you can camp at the beach, and it is supposed to be your private beach. The annoying part is, that other people don't respect that and walk right over your campsite and are sitting in front of your tent. If you bring your own Kayaks you can start right at your site. There are hiking trails starting at the campground, and my kids liked the Visitor Center a lot. Around sunrise you hear a buzzing over the lake. Those are millions of little fly, luckily they disappear during the day. Would I go again: Yes!

item.title: Mount Tamalpais SP: Campground Steep Ravine
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: If you like to stay on this campground, you need to book early. There are only 7 Campsite, every site has ocean view. Some sites have shade, some are in full sun. You can also rent a cabin, which is very close to the private beach. The campground is away from the street, and you can only drive down the road if you have a reservation and know the lock code at the gate.

item.title: Giant's Causeway: Ireland
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: If you visit Ireland, you definitely want to go to the giants causeway. It is about a 15min walk from the parking lot to the ocean, but they also have busses who can bring you down there. It is very impressive to see these large basalt columns going into the ocean, building little hills to climb on and also finding them in the surrounding Cliffs. Regardless of the weather, it is worth a trip.

item.title: Bumpass Hell: Lassen NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This is a easy 3 mi hike to a very unique spot in the middle of Lassen National Park. My kids enjoyed the different mud bubbles and tried to run away from the odor. The trail goes further then to this area, the 3 mi are up to the steam area and back.

item.title: Bodie - Ghost Town
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: I always wanted to go to see a ghost town, walking around, taking pictures and wondering what the story of the people who lived there was. But it came different then expected. There is a 3mi unpaved dirt road which brings you to Bodie, for some reason it took us a very long time to get there. Finally arrived we learned that we only have 15min left until they close. I took my camera and only make it to the first few houses. I hope I will go back on a not so hot day with more time.

item.title: Monolake
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: We saw a very large inviting looking lake from a restaurant close by. When we drove down to the lake, we saw a lot of black spots everywhere on the lake, can you guess what it is? We were very surprised to find out that there were millions of flys. I think that was the reason why we did not stay there very long. It was a lot of buzzing around you. A very interesting experience.

item.title: Yellowstone
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
This summer was the first time for me in Yellow stone, and I hope it was not the last. It was very impressive and diverse. This post is going to be the Yellowstone overview. Soon there will be more.
geothermal areas
Geysers 
lakes
meadows
waterfalls

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Would love to visit Yellowstone one day. Looks amazing.

item.title: Thunder Mountain Monument
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: Thunder Mountain Monument is built from items which were found in a 50mi radius of the monument. It was a very weird feeling to walk around the monument.

item.title: West Thump Geyser Basin: Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: This was a very easy and short hike to see a variety of geothermal basins. The walk is on wooden walkways and you get very close to the basins. You even see hot water bubbling in the yellowstone lake.

item.title: Bisons: Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
You get ready to go to Yellowstone and people tell you, there are so many Bisons..... We entered the park, and saw none! After two days my son pointed out of the window: "Mom is that a Bison? Is it real?" And it was.
This was the first we saw...
...then we were happy to see one on a meadow....
... on the street in front of us...
...a herd with a baby...
... then we realized they are everywhere. Each dark spot is a Bison.

item.title: Old Faithful - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
Went to  Yellowstone in June, because I read that July and August will be very busy. Well it was already very busy in June, and we did not have fun finding parking at Old Faithful. However, it is a very beautiful area to do small or longer hikes. We saw Old Faithful going off 3 Times.
Olf Faithful from the site where most people are
From the back side
While it is resting

item.title: Around Old Faithful - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
We took these pictures around Old Faithful from the wooden walkways. There are a lot of different Gysers, in different sizes. A few geothermal basins and Areas where Water flows in and out of a hole.
Water kept flowing in and out of the center of this area.

item.title: Bears are there. - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
You can see a lot of things when you open your eyes. These are bear paw print, next to a wooden walkway at Mud Volcano in Yellowstone.
deep bear paw prints, because the bear jumped down
unfortunately not very sharp, but the bear climbed over the fence and left some marks
more paw prints as he walked away

item.title: Lower Fall - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: There is a vista point to see the Waterfall from the distance. It is like a Drive In Waterfall Viewing.

item.title: Black Sand Basin - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
Black Sand Basin is a great Area to see geothermal ponds in different colors, small geysers and hot water floating into the river, without having too many people around you.
the wooden walk ways bring you from one nice area to the next
hot water flows into the river
I was amazed about the colors

item.title: Great Fountain Geyser: Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: The Great Fountain Geyser, is off the main road, and not so crowded as a lot of other places in Yellowstone. I don't know how busy it can be when it goes off...... It was beautiful to stay there and watch the moving clouds mirroring in the water.

item.title: Midway Geyser Basin - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded: There are so many places in Yellowstone National Park where you can see geothermal areas in different colors and sizes. The Midway Geyser Basin has is the largest in Yellowstone, but since you are on the same level, you are not able to see the whole area. Some people held up a tripod with an attached Camera, that way you get a better picture, but you don't see it. We saw people hiking on the little mountain behind the basin, I believe you get a great view from there. The hike's name is "picture hill".

item.title: Bald Eagles - Yellowstone NP
item.dc:creator: surroundyou
item.content:encoded:
I never saw a bald Eagle before and was hoping that we would see at least one. It was an amazing and exciting moment, seeing these birds. We stopped at this meadow, because there were lots of people, waiting at dusk for the wolves to come out. I was so glad we talked to them! This was our view. I did not expect to see a bald eagle sitting in a meadow. I learned on this trip, the more you talk to other people, the more you see. We met one family sitting and waiting with binoculars, we ask them what they were waiting for, and they let us see through their binoculars. It was focused on a peregrine falcon nest with chicks!
The last picture will show you where the bald eagle is, in case you don't find it.
and he is flying...
look out for droppings and you might find a nest or two...
the nests were in the rock wall on the left side of the waterfall.
did you see him before?
